item.title: Grid SVG barlines render duplicate glyphs (<use> plus legacy <text>)
item.justification: In `testing/grid-test.cho` section 2a, grid bar symbols render both the new SVG reference (`<use href="#bar-*" .../>`) and an additional legacy Unicode `<text>` glyph. Confirmed for single bar (`|`), double bar (`||`), and end bar (`|.`).

steps-to-reproduce.step: Use `testing/grid-test.cho` section 2a with `{start_of_grid shape="0+4x4+0"}` and `|: C . . . || Am . . . :| F . . . |. G . . . |`.
Generate HTML5 output and inspect the encoded grid SVG payload around barline tokens.

Observe duplicate output per barline token: e.g. `<use href="#bar-single" .../>` plus `<text ...>𝄀</text>`, `<use href="#bar-double" .../>` plus `<text ...>𝄃𝄂</text>`, and `<use href="#bar-end" .../>` plus `<text ...>𝄂</text>`.

item.expected-result: When icon symbols are emitted via `#bar-*`, no extra legacy Unicode `<text>` bar glyph should be emitted for the same bar token position.
item.analysis: Code evidence in `lib/ChordPro/Delegate/Strum/GridRenderer.pm` (`render_grid`, branch `if ($class eq 'bar')`) shows icon output via `_bar_use(...)`, followed by unconditional Unicode text output for gridline rows using `Tokens::bar_unicode($symbol)`. This creates duplicate barline rendering for all icon-backed bar symbols (single/double/end and repeat variants). Safe fix path: suppress plain bar Unicode text emission when icon-based `<use>` rendering is active, while retaining volta bracket text/labels.

tasks.task: Reproduce duplicate rendering for `|`, `||`, and `|.` in `testing/grid-test.cho` section 2a and capture rendered SVG evidence.
Adjust `lib/ChordPro/Delegate/Strum/GridRenderer.pm` so icon bar rendering (`_bar_use`) and legacy Unicode bar `<text>` do not render together for the same token.
Preserve volta bracket behavior (`data-volta` text/line rendering) and repeat semantics while removing duplicate plain bar glyph text.
Extend `t/92_html5_grid_bars.t` with assertions preventing duplicate Unicode bar glyphs when icon `<use href="#bar-*">` output exists.

technical-parameters.parameter: Do not regress repeat bars (`|:`, `:|`, `:|:`), end bar (`|.`), or volta bracket rendering.
Keep implementation localized to `lib/ChordPro/Delegate/Strum/GridRenderer.pm` and focused regression tests.

item.title: Strum modifier tokens miss dedicated Unicode glyph mapping in grid SVG
item.justification: In testing/grid-test.cho section 8e, many strum codes (da/ua/dx/ux/ds/us and + variants) do not render as dedicated symbols from ai-docs/Strum-requirement.md; output shows only partial generic arrows. Expected output should use explicit HTML-escaped symbols (e.g. ux+ => ↙).

steps-to-reproduce.step: Use `testing/grid-test.cho` section 8e and generate HTML5 output.
Inspect the produced grid SVG for line `|s da ua d+ u+ | dx ux ds us | da+ ua+ dx+ ux+ | ds+ us+ . . |`.
Compare rendered strum symbols against `ai-docs/Strum-requirement.md` symbol table (e.g. `ux+` expected as `↙`).
Observe that only partial generic arrows/decorations are present, while dedicated glyph mapping per modifier family is missing.

item.expected-result: All defined modifier families (`da/ua`, `d+/u+`, `dx/ux`, `ds/us`, `da+/ua+`, `dx+/ux+`, `ds+/us+`) render deterministic symbols according to requirement mapping, represented as HTML-escaped glyph content in SVG text nodes.
item.analysis:
Current implementation in `lib/ChordPro/Delegate/Strum/SVGPrimitives.pm` renders only a base up/down glyph (`gridstrum.symbols.up/down`) in `draw_arrow_svg()`. Modifier information (`muted`, `accent`, `staccato`, `arpeggio`) is added as separate decoration characters (`×`, `>`, `•`, `~`) rather than selecting a dedicated symbol per complete token (e.g. `ux+`).
Code evidence: `draw_arrow_svg()` computes glyph from direction only; `_strum_svg_decorations()` adds independent overlays. There is no token-to-glyph lookup table for full combinations in `SVGPrimitives.pm` or `Tokens.pm`. This explains why many variants appear as incomplete/partial symbols instead of the requirement-defined dedicated symbols.

Refactor `lib/ChordPro/Delegate/Strum/SVGPrimitives.pm::draw_arrow_svg` to render one deterministic mapped glyph per token instead of direction-only glyph plus ad hoc decorations.

item.title: Refactor strum bar-icon scaling to Y-only geometry
item.justification: Strum bar icons in `lib/ChordPro/Delegate/Strum/GridRenderer.pm::_bar_use` currently derive `width` from rendered `height` (`scaled_w = icon_w * (h / 100)`), causing X-thickness growth when bars span taller paired rows. This creates visually over-bold bars in strum contexts. The refactoring should decouple X and Y scaling so icon height remains dynamic while thickness in X stays stable and behavior-preserving.
item.analysis:
Current SVG emission in `_bar_use` applies proportional scaling from bar height to both dimensions. For paired grid+strum rows, `h` is larger than normal chord-row bars, which increases `scaled_w` and thickens bars unexpectedly. Desired structural change: keep X-width anchored to a constant baseline while continuing to stretch in Y to the required bar height.
This is a rendering-geometry refactor with no parser or token-model changes. Safe scope is limited to `GridRenderer.pm` and regression assertions for visual thickness stability.

Refactor sizing logic so X-width does not grow with bar height while Y scaling still follows row height.
Preserve existing bar-kind selection and symbol placement semantics (`single`, `double`, `end`, repeats, volta behavior).
Add focused tests that assert stable bar thickness in paired chord+strum rows and unchanged bar-kind rendering classes.

technical-parameters.parameter: Behavior-preserving refactor: no changes to token parsing, bar-kind detection, or workflow-log semantics.
Geometry decoupling: separate X-thickness policy from Y-height policy in `_bar_use` to avoid proportional-width inflation.

item.title: Standalone strum directives: full header grammar for start_of_strum/end_of_strum
item.justification: Current implementation parses standalone strum sections but only partially matches the requirement grammar in ai-docs/Strum-requirement.md for start_of_strum header with time signature, label, and optional tuplet. Add deterministic parsing for canonical header syntax and preserve existing key/value compatibility.
item.analysis:
Code inspection confirms `{start_of_strum}` and `{end_of_strum}` are implemented in `lib/ChordPro/Song.pm`, and `t/181_strum_sections.t` passes. The remaining requirement gap is canonical header grammar handling from `ai-docs/Strum-requirement.md` (`time-signature label [tuplet]`) as a first-class parse contract, not only as key/value fallback behavior.
The parser currently normalizes some forms via `parse_kv(..., "label")` and a regex that extracts `time_sig` from label prefixes. This should be formalized to support deterministic parsing and diagnostics for canonical syntax while retaining backwards compatibility for existing `label=...` and `tuplet=...` usage.

item.title: Combined modifier strum tokens (da+/dx+/ds+) render empty row in grid SVG
item.justification: In `testing/grid-test.cho` section 9 (`da+ ua+`, `dx+ ux+`, `ds+ us+`), generated HTML5 full-grid SVG keeps the paired strum row height but emits no strum symbols for the row. The same fixture renders arrows in section 7 and section 8, so this is a selective regression for combined modifier families.

steps-to-reproduce.step: Generate HTML5 output for `testing/grid-test.cho`: `perl -Ilib script/chordpro.pl testing/grid-test.cho --generate=HTML5 --output=testing/grid-test.html`.
Inspect section 9 comments: `9a - Arpeggio+accent (da+, ua+)`, `9b - Muted+accent (dx+, ux+)`, and `9c - Staccato+accent (ds+, us+)`.
Decode the corresponding `cp-grid-full-svg` payloads: each section has two-row height (`viewBox ... 58.00`) but no `<text ...>` strum symbols in the second row.
Cross-check parser output with JSON generation: `testing/grid-test.json` contains section-9 `strumline` tokens with names `da+`, `ua+`, `dx+`, `ux+`, `ds+`, `us+`.

item.expected-result: Section 9 strum rows render visible symbols for all combined modifiers (`da+/ua+`, `dx+/ux+`, `ds+/us+`) in full-grid SVG, consistent with section 8 behavior and the documented strum token matrix.
item.analysis:
Code evidence indicates a renderer-side token interpretation gap rather than parser loss. `testing/grid-test.json` confirms section-9 rows are parsed as `type="strumline"` and retain token names (`da+`, `ua+`, `dx+`, `ux+`, `ds+`, `us+`). Rendering path (`lib/ChordPro/Delegate/Strum/GridRenderer.pm`) calls `ChordPro::Delegate::Strum::Tokens::strum_symbol_info` for strum cells and only emits arrows when `direction` is detected.
In `lib/ChordPro/Delegate/Strum/Tokens.pm`, `strum_symbol_info` direction detection currently recognizes textual forms (`d`, `u`, `dn`, `up`) and a limited glyph subset (`↠|↣` down, `←|↖|↓` up). Section-9 tokens are normalized with symbol formats such as `↤` and `↔` (seen in `testing/grid-test.json` token payloads). These glyphs are not included in direction detection, so `direction` remains empty and the renderer emits no strum symbol, producing an apparently blank strum row.
Related item 76 addressed dedicated glyph mapping, but this issue is a distinct regression in direction normalization for glyph-form combined modifiers in the full-grid SVG path.

tasks.task: Reproduce section-9 blank-row symptom in `testing/grid-test.html` and capture decoded SVG evidence for missing strum symbols.
Extend `lib/ChordPro/Delegate/Strum/Tokens.pm::strum_symbol_info` direction detection to recognize glyph-form combined modifier symbols used by parser-normalized tokens (including `↤` and `↔`).
Keep canonical token code generation deterministic (`da+`, `ua+`, `dx+`, `ux+`, `ds+`, `us+`) so mapped glyph and fallback rendering remain consistent across grid and standalone paths.
Add mirrored regressions in `t/html5/09_bugfixes.t` and `t/190_html5_bugfixes.t` asserting that section-9 combined modifier rows emit visible strum symbols in decoded full-grid SVG payloads.

technical-parameters.parameter: Limit fix to strum token normalization/render contract (`Tokens.pm`) and mirrored regression suites.
Do not regress section 7/8 token families (`dn/up`, `d+/u+`, `dx/ux`, `da/ua`, `ds/us`) or existing gridline/chord rendering.

item.title: Repeat-bar tokens in |s rows shift strum symbols right in full-grid SVG
item.justification: In `testing/grid-test.cho` section 11a (`|: C . . . :| G . . . |` with `|s |: dn up dn up :| dn up dn up |`), the strum symbols in generated SVG appear optically shifted to the right (`x+`) relative to the chord-grid beat anchors.

steps-to-reproduce.step: Use `testing/grid-test.cho` section 11a and generate HTML5 output: `perl -Ilib script/chordpro.pl --nosongconfig testing/grid-test.cho --generate=HTML5 --output=testing/grid-test.html`.
Decode the section-11a `cp-grid-full-svg` payload and inspect strum-row text x-positions.
Observe first strum symbol starts at `x=60` while first beat/chord anchor is at `x=36`; later symbols continue with the same rightward bias.
Compare with the same gridline row anchors to verify repeat bars (`|:`, `:|`) are present but strum arrows are offset by one render column.

item.expected-result: In paired grid+strum full-grid SVG, strum symbols for `|s` rows with repeat bars align to the same beat columns as chord/grid anchors, without rightward drift.
item.analysis:
Code evidence points to column-accounting drift in `lib/ChordPro/Delegate/Strum/GridRenderer.pm::render_grid`. For paired rows, bars are drawn only on the gridline (`$is_paired_strumline` suppresses bar drawing on strum row), but the strum-row loop still increments `$column` for `class='bar'` tokens. In section 11a strum rows that explicitly include `|:` and `:|`, this consumes render columns before/inside strum beats and shifts subsequent arrow x-positions right.
Even though bar x-position uses canonical bar columns (`$canonical_bar_columns`), strum arrows are positioned from the evolving `$column` cursor. With hidden/suppressed strum-row bars, advancing `$column` on those bar tokens introduces an avoidable offset. Root-cause hypothesis: for paired strumline rows, bar tokens should anchor semantics without consuming arrow-placement columns, or an equivalent normalization step should decouple strum symbol columns from hidden bar tokens.

tasks.task: Reproduce section-11a drift and capture decoded SVG x-position evidence for chord anchors vs strum arrows.

Adjust `lib/ChordPro/Delegate/Strum/GridRenderer.pm` column progression so paired `strumline` bars (`|s` with `|:`, `:|`, `:|:`) do not shift arrow beat columns right when bar rendering is suppressed for that row.
Preserve repeat-bar semantics and canonical bar alignment across paired rows while removing arrow drift.
Add mirrored regression checks in `t/html5/09_bugfixes.t` and `t/190_html5_bugfixes.t` that assert section-11a strum symbol x-anchors align to intended beat columns.

Do not regress existing handling of `|S`/`|s`, repeat bars, end bars, or non-repeat strum rows.

item.title: Context-sensitive grid repeats: `%`/`%%` repeat chords on gridlines and strums on strumlines
item.justification: Chapter 12.6 and current parser behavior are misaligned for mixed grid+strum use cases. `%` and `%%` currently replay chord memory on gridlines, but in `|s` / `|S` rows they are effectively marker tokens without strum replay semantics. Requirement update: `%` repeats the previous bar in the same row context; `%%` repeats the previous two bars in the same row context. Therefore chord rows keep existing chord-repeat semantics while strum rows gain deterministic strum-pattern replay.
item.analysis: Code evidence in `lib/ChordPro/Song.pm` shows repeat parsing is unconditional (`repeat1`/`repeat2` token classes), but replay is currently tied to chord memory (`$memchords`, `$p0/$p1/$p2`) and gated away from strum rows (`!is_gridstrum($grid_type)`). As a result, strumline `%`/`%%` tokens do not replay prior strum bars. Rendering paths in `lib/ChordPro/Delegate/Strum/GridRenderer.pm` and `lib/ChordPro/Output/HTML5.pm` already understand repeat classes visually; the feature gap is semantic expansion and validation in parser state. Required implementation is a context-aware repeat memory model: chord history for gridlines, strum history for strumlines, with parse errors when history is insufficient.

tasks.task: Update requirement wording in `ai-docs/Grid-requirement.md` chapter 12.6 to specify context-sensitive `%`/`%%` semantics for gridline vs strumline rows and explicit insufficient-history error behavior.

item.title: Grid chord `%` slot counting diverges from strum `%` expansion, causing false mismatch errors
item.justification: Valid mixed grid+strum input in `testing/grid-test.cho` section 13b fails with `Strum line has 16 entries but chord line has 8 slots (mismatch)` although the chord row and strum row both represent four 4/4 measures. This blocks rendering for correct chart notation.

steps-to-reproduce.step: Use section 13b from `testing/grid-test.cho`: `|: C . . . | Am . . . | % | % :|` and `|s dn~up dn~up dn~up dn~up | dn~up dn~up dn~up dn~up | % | % |`.
Run: `perl -Ilib script/chordpro.pl testing/grid-test.cho --generate=HTML5 --output=testing/grid-test.html`.
Observe parser warning/error at line 314: `Strum line has 16 entries but chord line has 8 slots (mismatch)`.

item.expected-result: Section 13b parses successfully. Slot validation should treat chord `%`/`%%` measures consistently with strum `%`/`%%` replay semantics so equivalent four-measure lines do not fail mismatch checks.
item.analysis:
Code evidence in `lib/ChordPro/Song.pm` (`decompose_grid`) shows slot validation compares `$nbt` for strum rows against `$grid_last_slot_count` from previous chord row. In the current repeat implementation, strum `%`/`%%` paths expand into replayed tokens and explicitly increment `$nbt` (e.g., `+$scalar(@expanded)`), while chord `%`/`%%` keep marker tokens and update chord memory but do not increase `$nbt`. For section 13b this yields `$grid_last_slot_count=8` (explicit two bars only) versus strum `$nbt=16` after replay expansion, producing a false-positive mismatch.
This is adjacent to item 81 behavior: context-sensitive repeats were added, but validation accounting remained asymmetric between chord and strum contexts. Existing tests cover `%` with plain `dn up` bars, but do not cover `%` replay with sub-beat strum cells (`dn~up`) against chord-line `%` markers in the same grid block.

tasks.task: Reproduce section 13b mismatch and capture parser-state evidence for `$nbt` and `$grid_last_slot_count` divergence at validation.
Adjust `lib/ChordPro/Song.pm` slot accounting so chord-line `%`/`%%` contribute equivalent slot counts for validation purposes, consistent with strum replay expansion.
Ensure fix preserves current chord token output semantics (`repeat1`/`repeat2`) and does not regress chord-memory behavior.
Add parser regression in `t/180_grids.t` using a section-13b-like case with `dn~up` and `%` on both rows; assert no mismatch error.
Add mirrored HTML5 regressions in `t/html5/09_bugfixes.t` and `t/190_html5_bugfixes.t` validating successful render of this mixed repeat/sub-beat case.

technical-parameters.parameter: Limit change to parser slot-count validation and targeted regressions.
Do not regress existing `%`/`%%` rendering output, repeat markers, or mismatch diagnostics for genuinely invalid strum/chord width differences.

item.title: Chord `%%` two-measure repeat triggers false `Too few cells` warning in valid 4x4 grids
item.justification: Valid ChordPro input using `%%` as a two-measure repeat emits warnings in `testing/grid-test.cho` section 4c (line 100 and mirrored line 366): `Too few cells for grid content`. The line is valid and should repeat the previous two bars without warning.

steps-to-reproduce.step: Use section 4c: `{start_of_grid shape="0+4x4+0"}` `| C . . . | Am . . . | %% | . . . . |`.
Run: `perl -Ilib script/chordpro.pl testing/grid-test.cho --generate=HTML5 --output=testing/grid-test.html`.
Observe warnings: `line 100, Too few cells for grid content` `line 366, Too few cells for grid content`.

item.expected-result: For valid two-measure repeat notation with `%%`, parser should not emit `Too few cells for grid content` warnings.
item.analysis:
After item 82, parser used one counter (`$nbt`) for both visual cell-capacity checks and semantic repeat-width validation. In `lib/ChordPro/Song.pm::decompose_grid`, chord `%%` was charged with semantic width to maintain strum/chord parity, but that same charged value was also used for `Too few cells` checks against grid shape capacity. This incorrectly flagged valid `%%` rows as oversized.
Root cause: conflated responsibilities in one counter. Correct model requires separate counters: visual token width for shape-capacity checks vs semantic slot width for repeat parity validation.

item.title: Chord grid `%` and `%%` still render literal markers instead of repeated bar content
item.justification: In `testing/grid-test.cho`, sections 15c/15d still show literal `%` and `%%` in generated SVG. Reported expectation is that these markers should be replaced by the repeated content of the previous one or two bars, not displayed as marker symbols.

steps-to-reproduce.step: Use `testing/grid-test.cho` sections 15c and 15d: `| C . . . | Am . . . | % | % |` `| C . . . | Am . . . | %% | . . . . |`.
Run: `perl -Ilib script/chordpro.pl testing/grid-test.cho --generate=HTML5 --output=testing/grid-test.html`.
Inspect the generated full-grid SVG rows for those sections and observe `%`/`%%` symbols are rendered as visible text tokens.

item.expected-result: For chord grid rows, `%` should render as the previous bar content and `%%` as the previous two bars, so final visual output shows repeated chord content instead of literal `%`/`%%` symbols.
item.analysis:
Code evidence indicates this is currently expected by implementation, but conflicts with the newly reported output expectation.
In `lib/ChordPro/Song.pm::decompose_grid`, chord-row `%`/`%%` still create marker tokens (`class="repeat1"` / `class="repeat2"`) with `symbol` set to `%`/`%%` while replay state is used for semantic accounting and chord memory, not display-token replacement.
In `lib/ChordPro/Delegate/Strum/GridRenderer.pm`, gridline rendering explicitly maps `repeat1`/`repeat2` to `$token->{symbol}` text output, so the SVG intentionally paints `%`/`%%` literals.
Items 81/82/83 explicitly preserved marker rendering semantics, so this is not a duplicate defect but a new behavior-change bug against current user expectation. Fix likely requires parser normalization and/or renderer display substitution for chord repeat markers while retaining strum-row replay behavior and slot-validation correctness.

Update `lib/ChordPro/Delegate/Strum/GridRenderer.pm` gridline rendering to emit resolved repeat content for chord rows, not literal `%`/`%%`, while keeping bar alignment stable.
Keep item-82/item-83 slot-validation invariants intact (no mismatch regressions, no false `Too few cells` warnings).
Add parser regression coverage in `t/180_grids.t` for sections 15c/15d asserting resolved-repeat display tokens are present and literal `%`/`%%` are absent in chord rows.
Add mirrored HTML5 regressions in `t/html5/09_bugfixes.t` and `t/190_html5_bugfixes.t` validating section 15c/15d SVG output uses repeated chord content.
